maya: Heads up — after enabling the new mix-quant profile `mix-4fp8-v2` for rw-llama-13b on Dedicated we see a regression in quality. Eval job 2026-03-17-901 shows hallucination rate +3.7pp and several structured JSON outputs missing keys (examples below). Also noticed a tail latency bump. :eyes:

maya: Example bad output (expected structured):
```json
{"title":"...","items":[{"id":123,"name":"foo"}, ...]}
```
was returned as:
```json
{"items":[{"name":"foo"}], "error":null}
```

alex: Thanks, can you paste the eval job id + any runtime logs? Is this only on long-ctx requests or all traffic?

maya: job id = 2026-03-17-901 (same as above). Repro curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.internal/generate` (payload contains structured schema prompt + examples). Failure rate much higher when seq_len > 1024. Attached snippets from the runtime log for a failing request: `kernel_select: chosen=int4_fast, fallback_chain=[int4_fast->fp8_slow], kv_cache_hit=false, batch_size=8, pad_to=2048`

ben: Pasted profiler snippet from a short perf-run: 
```
LAYER_RANGE  KERNEL        LAT(ms)  TOK/s    SCALE_TYPE
0-8         fp8_safe      1.2      1900     per-tensor
9-22        int4_fast     0.45     5200     per-channel
23-40       int4_fast     0.48     5100     per-channel
fallbacks    fp8_slow     2.6      500      per-tensor
KV_CACHE_MISS_RATIO: baseline=0.011 -> current=0.072
SCHED_DECISIONS: prefer_latency_weights -> chose int4_fast for mixed layers when seq>1024
```
Ben: Notable: scheduler is binding to int4_fast for many mid layers to hit latency SLOs. When batcher pads to 2048 the KV offsets get larger and we see more fallback to fp8_slow in the middle of generation which appears to correlate with scaled-value drift.

sara: My hypothesis: calibration mismatch between per-channel int4 scales and per-tensor fp8 fallback path. When a fallback happens mid-generation we don't correctly rescale the cached KV entries, so subsequent decode steps operate on inconsistent magnitudes -> structured field tokens become scrambled and hallucinate. Also batching heuristic pads aggressively which increases probability of crossing the kernel-selection threshold so more fallbacks.

sara: Quick checks to run: 1) run `calib-compare --baseline calib-v1 --target mix-4fp8-v2 --dataset eval-schema` and diff per-layer scales, 2) confirm KV cache versioning header is present in logs (should be kv-v2), 3) repro with batch_size=1 and no pad_to to isolate padding effect.

alex: Mitigation proposal: toggle routing to prefer fp8 for longctx and disable aggressive pad_to for the canary. Example runtime override: `routing.policy.longctx_preference=fp8_safe` and `batcher.pad_to=auto` (we can flip via --runtime-flag on the service). Can we do that quickly as a hotfix?

maya: I'll open a canary and run the repro with `pad_to=auto` and `routing.policy.longctx_preference=fp8_safe`. Starting now.

eng-bot: deploy: canary rollout started by maya for service=rw-llama-13b pool=dedicated-canary at 2183350005 :rocket:

ben: I'll run the calib-compare and post diffs here. If diffs show per-channel shifts > 0.02 we should revert mix-4fp8-v2 for the wider fleet.

sara: I can look at the KV cache code path — quick suspicion is missing scale-tag when copying cached KV between kernels. Will triage after I finish current oncall.

maya: Thanks — tagging @alex @ben @sara. Meeting in 30m to decide rollback if canary doesn't improve. :thumbsup:
